items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A roundabout puzzle opens the lesson: the speedometer never moves, so **is the car accelerating?**

One athlete on a circular track then carries the idea — her distance and displacement, her speed, and why her velocity keeps changing although her speed does not.

We end with numericals from the whole chapter.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• distance and displacement

• average speed and average velocity

• acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time, and velocity has a direction

• circumference of a circle = $2\pi r$

• the three equations of motion

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Explain why uniform circular motion is accelerated motion.

**2.** Find the speed in circular motion, $v = \dfrac{2\pi r}{T}$.

**3.** Give everyday examples of circular motion.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• A car going round a roundabout, seen from above.

• Its speedometer reads a steady **36 km/h** all the way round.

**Answer to Question 1**

**No.** It stays at 36 km/h the whole way round.

**Answer to Question 2**

Take a quick poll. Most will say no. **Do not reveal the answer yet.**

**Answer to Question 3**

When the **velocity** changed. Let them guess what might be changing here.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• A circular track of radius **70 m**. Take $\pi = \tfrac{22}{7}$.

• The athlete starts at **A** and runs at a steady pace, A → B → C → D → A.

• **B** is a quarter round, **C** is half a round.

**Answer to Question 4**

The circumference: $2\pi r = 2\times\dfrac{22}{7}\times 70 = 440\ \text{m}$.

**Answer to Question 5**

**Zero.** She is back at A.

**Answer to Question 6**

Distance $=$ half the circumference $= 220\ \text{m}$. Displacement $=$ the straight line AC $=$ the diameter $= 140\ \text{m}$, from A towards C.

**Answer to Question 7**

Distance $= 110\ \text{m}$. Displacement $=$ the straight line AB, about $99\ \text{m}$ — shorter than the arc.

script.x: Show the track. Pointer 1 sets up the radius and the lettering.
Questions 4 to 7 in order. Answers are on pointers 2 to 5.
Show the conclusion box.

After 3 full rounds of a track of radius r, an athlete's displacement and distance travelled are

items.text:
**On Question 1**

Distance $=\pi r = \dfrac{22}{7}\times 7 = 22\ \text{m}$; displacement $=$ diameter $= 14\ \text{m}$.

chunks.name: How fast does she go round?

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The same track, now with her stopwatch.

• **22 s** at B, **44 s** at C, **66 s** at D, **88 s** back at A.

**Answer to Question 8**

$110\ \text{m}$ each time — equal distances in equal intervals, so her speed is **constant**.

**Answer to Question 9**

$\dfrac{440}{88} = 5\ \text{m/s}$. Any quarter gives the same: $\dfrac{110}{22} = 5\ \text{m/s}$.

**Answer to Question 10**

**Zero**, because her displacement is zero.

items.prompt: The second hand of a wall clock is 21 cm long. The speed of its tip is
Arjun and Kabir cycle round the same circular track. Arjun takes 40 s per round and Kabir takes 60 s. Who is faster, and by how much?

items.text:
**On Question 1**

In 60 s the tip covers $2\pi r = 2\times\dfrac{22}{7}\times 21 = 132\ \text{cm}$, so $v = \dfrac{132}{60} = 2.2\ \text{cm/s}$.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Three tracks: a rectangle, a hexagon and a circle.

• The marks show where a runner has to change direction.

**Answer to Question 11**

Take a quick poll and come back to it at the end of this part.

**Answer to Question 12**

**4 times** on the rectangle and **6 times** on the hexagon.

**Answer to Question 13**

The turns come closer and closer together. On a circle the direction changes at **every point**, continuously.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Left: the velocity arrow at several points on the circle.

• Right: a stone whirled on a string, released at **P**, and the path it takes after.

**Answer to Question 14**

Along the line that just touches the circle at that point — the **tangent** — in the direction of motion.

**Answer to Question 15**

**Straight along the tangent at P.** That shows its velocity at P was along the tangent.

script.x: Show the figure. Pointer 1 names the two halves.
Questions 14 and 15. Answers are on pointers 2 and 3.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The velocity at **P** and at **Q**, drawn side by side.

• Same arrow length means the same speed; different directions mean different velocities.

**Answer to Question 16**

**Yes.** The arrows have the same length.

**Answer to Question 17**

**No.** They point in different directions.

**Answer to Question 18**

**Yes.** The velocity changes because its *direction* changes, even though the speed does not.

items.prompt: A ball tied to a string moves anticlockwise in a circle. Which arrow shows its velocity at P?

items.text:
**On this question**

The velocity is along the **tangent** at P, in the direction of motion.

items.prompt: Assertion (A): A car taking a circular turn at a steady 36 km/h has zero acceleration.  Reason (R): The speed of the car does not change during the turn.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

items.prompt: A girl's scooter shows a constant speedometer reading. Can her scooter still be accelerating?
options: No — constant speed means no acceleration
Yes — if she is taking a turn, the direction of her velocity changes
Yes — but only if she brakes
No — scooters cannot accelerate on a turn

items.text:
**On Question 1**

R is true, but the **direction** of the velocity changes, so the car is accelerated. A is false.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Six everyday things: a ceiling fan, a wall clock, a merry-go-round, a satellite, a giant wheel and a swing.

**Answer to Question 19**

The **tip of a fan blade** at full speed, the **tips of the clock hands**, and a **merry-go-round** turning steadily.

**Answer to Question 20**

**Very nearly.** Their paths are almost circular and their speeds almost constant.

**Answer to Question 21**

**No.** It moves in a circle, but its speed is increasing.

**Answer to Question 22**

**No.** It moves back and forth along part of a circle and never goes round.

items.prompt: Which is the odd one out?
options: the tip of the second hand of a clock
a satellite in a circular orbit
a car speeding up as it goes round a roundabout

items.text:
**On this question**

Its **speed changes**, so its circular motion is not uniform.
